articles.title: Modeling Signal Towers as Typed Entities: GenAnywhere's Content Architecture for Sites, Structures, and Spectrum Paths
articles.excerpt: A signal tower site looks like a single object from the highway and becomes a graph the moment you open its file. The foundation anchors a structure; the structure carries frames; frames carry antenna…
articles.body: A signal tower site looks like a single object from the highway and becomes a graph the moment you open its file. The foundation anchors a structure; the structure carries frames; frames carry antennas and dishes; antennas own azimuths and coverage polygons; dishes own paths to distant endpoints; cables bind radios in shelters to everything above; and a regulatory envelope wraps the whole assembly in lighting, marking, and consultation obligations. GenAnywhere, the content-shaping persona we use for infrastructure platforms, models this graph explicitly as typed entities so that every paragraph, checklist, and drawing reference in a tower document resolves against one structure. This post walks the model, its invariants, and its renderers in plain language.

articles.body: Rowflare is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) Airtable alternative. The whole app is one Cloudflare Worker plus one Durable Object class: every base gets its own Durable Object, and that object owns a private SQLite database with all of the base's tables, fields, views and rows. browser -- HTTP -- > Worker ( auth , routing , REST API , assets ) -- RPC -- > Base Durable Object ( one per base ) ^ | | SQLite : tables , fields , views , rows + ------ WebSocket -------- + ---------------------------------------- -+ alarm : batch jobs D1 : users , workspaces , members , tokens R2 : attachments The Worker handles sessions, personal access tokens, workspaces and roles (in D1), the REST API, uploads to R2 and the static web app.

articles.title: Docker for Developers Who Don't Want to Become DevOps Engineers
articles.excerpt: Docker can look intimidating at first. Images, containers, volumes, networks, registries, Dockerfiles... The basic idea is actually simple: Package an application together with the environment it need…
articles.body: Docker can look intimidating at first. Images, containers, volumes, networks, registries, Dockerfiles... The basic idea is actually simple: Package an application together with the environment it needs to run. The "Works on My Machine" Problem Imagine your application requires: Node.js 22 MongoDB Specific npm dependencies Environment variables A teammate might have: Node.js 20 Different MongoDB version Different operating system Problems appear. Docker helps standardize the environment. Dockerfile A basic Node.js Dockerfile might look like: FROM node:22 WORKDIR /app COPY package*.json ./ RUN npm install COPY . . EXPOSE 3000 CMD ["npm", "start"] This describes how the application environment should be created. Image vs Container An image is the packaged blueprint.

articles.title: Does your coding agent remember yesterday? I measured: 0/10 without memory, 10/10 with it — and three bugs on the way

articles.body: We wrote "memory carries across sessions" in the skillmem README and in every post about it. We never measured it. This week I did, on my own working database. Here is what came out, including the parts that don't flatter us. skillmem is local memory for coding agents: SQLite, nine mem_* MCP tools and Claude Code hooks. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other clients can share one database. Test 1: does a fresh window remember the old one? Window 1 gets a decision: "the Arka release moves to November 14, codename Falcon, owner Timur." The window closes. Window 2, a new session, is asked: "what's the codename and who owns it?" Five scenarios, two runs each. The agent is claude -p with clean settings: no CLAUDE.md and no built-in auto-memory. One arm has skillmem wired in, the other doesn't.

articles.title: Resize Images for Any Platform Without Uploading: A Browser-Only Guide
articles.excerpt: Every creator knows the pain: each platform wants a different image size. Instagram 1080x1080, TikTok 1080x1920, Twitter 1600x900, YouTube 1280x720, LinkedIn 1200x627... Resizing one photo for five pl…
articles.body: Every creator knows the pain: each platform wants a different image size. Instagram 1080x1080, TikTok 1080x1920, Twitter 1600x900, YouTube 1280x720, LinkedIn 1200x627... Resizing one photo for five platforms usually means opening an editor, remembering each spec, and exporting five times. Worse, most online "resize" tools upload your image to a server first - which is slow, and a privacy concern if the photo isn't meant to leave your device. That's why I built imgsize , a 100% browser-based image resizer. Your image never leaves your device. Pick a platform preset (70+ included), and it's resized instantly with the exact dimensions that platform wants. Why browser-only processing matters No uploads - your photos stay on your device.

articles.body: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated. Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). Node.js disclosed the flaw

articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.body: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s symposium is focused on humanity’s return to the Moon, sustainable lunar infrastructure, advanced space propulsion, and the evolving space workforce. Panels include discussions on Artemis II and III, space propulsion flash talks, building utilities and infrastructure for sustainable lunar operations, Moon base supply chain resilience, space nuclear technology, navigating the new NASA workforce, and engineering the future, featuring keynotes and awards presentations.
articles.author: Lee Mohon

articles.title: Spiral’s Edge
articles.excerpt: This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released on Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, t…
articles.body: NASA, ESA, Michael Jones (California Institute of Technology); Image Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released on Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way-like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth. Low-mass galaxies like the ones in this Hubble observing program provide a way to test the predictions of cosmological models on small scales, which struggle to match observations.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.

articles.title: After Starshield interruption, Ukraine wants to build its own satellite communication network with ICEYE and Nokia
articles.excerpt: Ukraine's military just signed a letter of intent with Nokia and the Finnish satellite maker ICEYE to look into developing a sovereign satellite-communication system for the war-torn nation.
articles.body: Ukraine wants its own satellite-communication system, which shouldn't be surprising given the events of the past week or so. The Ukrainian military just signed a letter of intent with two Finnish companies — the telecom giant Nokia and satellite maker ICEYE — to look into developing a sovereign satellite-communications network for Ukraine. "Ukraine needs secure, sovereign and high-performance satellite communications systems that it controls," ICEYE cofounder and CEO Rafal Modrzewski said in a statement today (Oct. 22). "We have a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions at speed to help build that capability.

articles.body: Right now, there is probably an AI agent running on a laptop somewhere in your network. It stores API keys and database passwords, can access your internal systems, and works without anyone watching. Nobody reviewed its access. Nobody owns it. If an employee had that much reach with that little oversight, you would call it an insider risk. So why do we still call the agent a productivity tool?
